note: CS2 inherited its launch-option parser from Source 2, and most of the folklore still circulating online is Source 1 advice that CS:GO honoured and CS2 silently drops. Status values: 'good' (does what people think), 'situational' (real effect, only sometimes wanted), 'dead' (parsed and ignored, harmless clutter), 'harmful' (measurably worse), 'invalid' (not a real flag). Confidence says how sure the entry is; 'medium' entries are worth re-checking after a major game update.

-novid.reason: Skips the intro movie. Saves a couple of seconds every launch.

-console.reason: Opens the developer console at startup. Required if your config relies on console access.

-fullscreen.reason: Forces exclusive fullscreen, which is the lowest-latency present mode.

-windowed.reason: Windowed mode. Costs latency versus exclusive fullscreen; only useful when you need to alt-tab constantly.

-noborder.reason: Removes the window border. Pairs with -windowed for borderless.

-w.reason: Render width. Combined with -h this pins the resolution regardless of what the video config says.

-refresh.reason: Pins the refresh rate. Worth setting explicitly when Windows keeps dropping the panel to 60 Hz.

-freq.reason: Older alias for -refresh. Harmless, but -refresh is the current spelling.

+exec.reason: Executes a config file at startup. This is how an autoexec gets loaded reliably.

-allow_third_party_software.reason: Lets overlay and capture software inject. Needed by some streaming tools; leave it off otherwise.

-high.reason: Starts the process at high priority. On older homogeneous CPUs this can help slightly. On Intel hybrid P/E-core parts it can fight the Thread Director and land the hot render thread badly, so this tool leaves it off there.

-full.reason: Not a real flag. The option you want is -fullscreen; -full is silently discarded.

-nojoy.reason: CS:GO used this to skip loading joystick support and save a little memory. CS2 does not read it.

-d3d9ex.reason: A Direct3D 9 path that only ever existed in Source 1. CS2 renders on Direct3D 11 / Vulkan.

-tickrate.reason: CS2 uses sub-tick updates, so there is no tickrate to set. In CS:GO this only ever affected locally hosted servers anyway, never matchmaking.

-threads.reason: Overrides the engine's worker thread count. CS2 sizes its job pool from the actual topology; pinning it to a hand-picked number usually costs frames, and on a hybrid CPU it can starve the render thread outright.

-forcenovsync.reason: Source 1. Turn V-Sync off in the video settings instead.

-lv.reason: Low-violence mode from Source 1; CS2 has no equivalent switch here.

-vulkan.reason: Selects the Vulkan backend. Linux only; ignored on Windows.

-insecure.reason: Disables VAC. You cannot play on secure servers. Never added automatically.

-perfectworld.reason: Perfect World client, for mainland China accounts.

+mat_queue_mode.reason: A Source 1 multithreaded material system toggle. The convar does not exist in CS2, so this does nothing.

+cl_updaterate.reason: Removed with the move to sub-tick networking.

+cl_cmdrate.reason: Removed with the move to sub-tick networking.

+cl_interp.reason: Interpolation is handled by the engine in CS2; the old manual tuning no longer applies.

+rate.reason: Still a real convar, but CS2 defaults to 786432 and the value carried over from CS:GO guides (128000) is a large downgrade in bandwidth ceiling. Leave it at the default unless a genuinely narrow connection forces otherwise.

+fps_max.reason: Better set in a config than on the command line, so it can be changed without editing Steam.
